methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI pressure on young workers without corresponding depth-building infrastructure signals shallow adoption anxiety rather than capability development, potentially creating workforce displacement without retraining pathways in Virginia's secondary tech hub.

signals.title: EPA grant backs community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia - Virginia Tech News
signals.signal_reading: EPA-funded community-driven workforce training in Southwest Virginia represents distributed capacity-building through place-based education, potentially creating deep technical skills outside traditional metro concentrations if sustained beyond grant cycles.

signals.title: Hampton Roads taking steps to prepare for data centers - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: Hampton Roads preparing for data centers signals infrastructure-led concentration rather than human capability distribution—physical AI infrastructure attracts capital but doesn't inherently build regional technical depth unless coupled with workforce development.

signals.title: Pentagon Expands Scale AI Deal to $500M and AI Defense Firm TurbineOne Moves HQ to Northern Virginia - Clearance Jobs
signals.signal_reading: Pentagon's $500M Scale AI expansion and TurbineOne HQ relocation to NoVA intensifies defense-AI capability concentration in the already-dominant corridor, widening the talent and capital gap between Northern Virginia and the rest of the Commonwealth.

signals.title: Data or Water? Safety or Privacy? Roanoke Faces Tradeoffs as New Technology and Legislation Reshape Daily Life - The Roanoke Rambler
signals.signal_reading: Public deliberation over data center tradeoffs in Roanoke signals civic AI literacy development—communities wrestling with technology governance questions demonstrate emerging distributed fluency beyond just deployment or consumption.
